geometry_source: B3LYP/6-31G* and CASSCF/6-31G* optimizations/frequency characterizations of ground-state reactant/products, triplet and singlet biradicals, conformers, and transition states; B3LYP IRC for one transition state
method: CASSCF(4,4), CASSCF(6,6), and CASSCF(8,8) mechanistic calculations compared with unrestricted/restricted B3LYP
active_space_orbital_description: For triplet t3 conformers, CAS(4,4) contains pi/pi-star of the newly formed C1-C2 pi bond and sigma/sigma-star of C2-C3; CAS(6,6) adds sigma/sigma-star of C1-O; CAS(8,8) further adds the C3- and N-centered nonbonding orbitals carrying the odd electrons. For [2+2] t2 formation, CAS(6,6) contains sigma/sigma-star of the forming C3-C4 bond, the C2/C5 odd-electron orbitals, and pi/pi-star of C2-C3. For [3+2] path a it instead includes forming N6-C4 sigma/sigma-star, C2/C5 radical orbitals, and C2-C3 pi/pi-star; path b uses forming C3-C4 sigma/sigma-star, C5/N6 radical orbitals, and the same C2-C3 pi pair.
active_space_protocol: The four t3 conformers were explicitly checked with nested CAS(4,4), (6,6), and (8,8) spaces; relative ordering is stable except that the largest space increases the penalty for d-t3. Production reaction-path stationary points and singlet-triplet gaps use CAS(6,6). The source describes optimized state-specific stationary points and does not report state averaging or multiple roots in one optimization.
nroots_per_mult: one targeted singlet or triplet root for each reactant, biradical, conformer, or transition structure
electronic_structure_description: CASSCF(6,6) places the hydrogen-shifted triplet t3 6.81 kcal/mol below t1 and gives adiabatic 1-to-t1 and 1-to-t3 excitation energies of 59.37 and 52.56 kcal/mol. Across CAS(4,4)/(6,6)/(8,8), doubly hydrogen-bonded a-t3 remains the lowest of four t3 conformers; b-, c-, and d-t3 lie 3.16, 26.60, and 16.77 kcal/mol above it at CAS(8,8). For ethylene addition, CASSCF(6,6) transition barriers are 13.2-13.9 kcal/mol on the t1 [2+2] channel; on the t3 [3+2] channel, N attack (16.0-16.3) is lower than C3 attack (18.4-18.8). Optimized singlet biradicals lie much higher (18.3-21.1 relative to the corresponding triplet reactant-plus-ethylene references), leading the authors to favor triplet cyclization.
Other: The photoexcited quinone, t1-to-t3 hydrogen shift, four t3 conformers, six ethylene-attack conformers per channel, all transition structures, singlet/triplet biradicals, fragmentation alternatives, and three final cycloadduct connectivities are consolidated as one overall fixed-reactant reaction system. Important caveats: the paper calls unrestricted-B3LYP singlet biradicals with <S^2> near 1.0 'pure singlets,' although a spin-pure singlet has <S^2>=0; those broken-symmetry DFT states are substantially spin contaminated. No spin-orbit coupling, minimum-energy crossing seam, or ISC rate is computed, so the claim that intersystem crossing is impossible follows only from energy differences. The conclusion that gauche-out is always most stable is also not supported uniformly by the CASSCF tables: for t2 and path-a t4, the CASSCF intermediate energies are lowest for anti, while only the t2 formation barrier slightly favors gauche-out. Ground-state product stabilization energies (-20.7, -2.6, +1.7 kcal/mol) are B3LYP-only and not separate entries.

CASSCF/CASPT2 calculations are single points on DFT geometries.
method: M06-2X, BP86, and B97D geometry/frequency calculations followed by CASSCF and CASPT2 spin-state energetics and vertical spectra; Cholesky-decomposed two-electron integrals
software: Gaussian 09 for DFT; MOLCAS 7 for CASSCF/CASPT2
basis_set: DFT: TZVP on Ni and SVP on other atoms, with all-atom-TZVP checks. Multireference: ANO-RCC-TZVP on Ni and N, ANO-RCC-DZ on peripheral C/F/H, and ANO-RCC-TZVP on PAPy carbon atoms
active_space_orbital_description: Primary spin-state space: eight Ni(II) 3d electrons plus two electrons in an equatorial porphyrin-N sigma-donor combination, distributed over five predominantly Ni 3d orbitals, their five diffuse 4d-like double-shell partners, and the porphyrin-N sigma orbital. The ESI plots every orbital. A CAS(12,12) test adds both equatorial and axial sigma-donor orbitals to the double d shell in five-coordinate species. The optical CAS(10,8) instead contains four porphyrin/PAPy bonding pi or N-lone-pair orbitals and four antibonding orbitals, omitting metal-centered excitations.
active_space_protocol: CAS(10,11)/CASPT2 single points compare singlet and triplet roots of trans-sqp, trans-spy, and cis-spy on M06-2X geometries. CAS(12,12) checks the singlet-triplet splittings of the two five-coordinate conformers without unbalancing the four-coordinate complex. A separate state-averaged CAS(10,8)/CASPT2 treatment gives the spin-allowed vertical spectrum of trans-sqp; four reported excited singlet states describe the Q/near-UV region. All conformers, coordination numbers, spin roots, dissociation-scan geometries, active-space tests, and DFT variants are consolidated into this one chemical row.
nroots_per_mult: One low-spin singlet and one high-spin triplet per coordination conformer for spin energetics; at least four singlet vertical excited roots in the CAS(10,8) spectrum
electronic_structure_description: Four-coordinate square-planar Ni(II) has paired d8 electrons and a singlet ground state, whereas axial pyridyl coordination narrows the 3dz2/3dx2-y2 gap and stabilizes a triplet square-pyramidal state. Dispersion-driven porphyrin-PAPy stacking mixes the accepting porphyrin pi-star and azo pi-star character. The calculated Q-band promotion therefore weakens N=N and can trigger trans-to-cis isomerization, after which pyridyl-N coordination locks the high-spin form. Intersystem crossing is part of the proposed mechanism, but no explicit spin-orbit matrix elements are computed.
Other: M06-2X places cis-spy triplet at 0.00 eV, trans-spy at 0.28, trans-sqp at 0.42, trans-sqp-open at 0.72, cis-sqp at 0.91, and cis-sqp-open at 1.32. CAS(10,11)/CASPT2 energies relative to cis-spy triplet are: trans-sqp singlet/triplet 0.26/0.39 eV, cis-spy singlet/triplet 1.07/0.00, and trans-spy singlet/triplet 1.32/0.29; CAS(12,12) preserves the five-coordinate ordering. Trans-spy pyridine dissociation is nearly barrierless, while cis-spy rises by 0.84 eV at Ni-N=3.3 A, excluding a stable all-trans switching mechanism. The two lowest CAS(10,8)/CASPT2 Q-band excitations are 2.59 and 2.65 eV with oscillator strengths 0.0370 and 0.0560 and populate mixed porphyrin/azo antibonding orbitals. A direct azo pi-to-pi-star root is near 7.25 eV at SA-CASSCF and suffers severe CASPT2 intruder states, so it cannot explain 500-nm switching.

For 2A2 the out-of-plane pi space is strongly delocalized, but adding in-plane degrees of freedom can reintroduce lower Cs solutions, so the true symmetry remains uncertain.

geometry_source: Ground-state neutral and cation equilibrium structures and cation normal modes were optimized by B3LYP/aug-cc-pVTZ (H,C,Br)/aug-cc-pVTZ-PP (I). Appendix 2 gives neutral/cation r(C-I)=2.156/2.154 A, r(C-Br)=1.944/1.938, r(C-H)=1.080/1.082, angle I-C-Br=114.87/95.48 degrees and H-C-H=112.39/116.27. method: single-state CASSCF for neutral and five-state-averaged CASSCF for cation potential/dipole/SOC curves; one-dimensional time-dependent wavepacket propagation with explicit SOC and strong-field coupling; B3LYP/TDDFT comparison model
software: MOLCAS 7.2 for SA-CASSCF/SOC; Gaussian 03 for B3LYP geometries and normal modes; Fourier-grid/Split-Operator quantum dynamics implementation
basis_set: CASSCF: ANO-RCC contracted to TZP, H 3s2p1d, C 4s3p2d1f, Br 6s5p3d2f1g, I 6s5p3d2f1g; DFT geometry/model: aug-cc-pVTZ for H,C,Br and aug-cc-pVTZ-PP for I

The five cation diabats are dominated by one hole/singly occupied orbital in 4a-prime, 2a-double-prime, 3a-prime, 1a-double-prime and 2a-prime, respectively; the 5a-prime and 6a-prime sigma-star orbitals are empty while remaining active orbitals are doubly occupied.
active_space_protocol: The neutral ground curve is single-state CAS(12,8); the five lowest doublet cation curves use equal five-state averaging in CAS(11,8). Diabatic CASSCF potentials, coordinate-dependent transition dipoles and AMFI SOC elements are transformed to adiabatic curves and propagated as one singlet-neutral plus five doublets for each ms=+/-1/2 (eleven electronic components total). All charge stages, states, scan points, field strengths and photodissociation products are consolidated as one reaction/dynamics system rather than split into intermediate-state rows.
nroots_per_mult: one neutral singlet root; five state-averaged cation doublet roots, doubled into ten ms/SOC components
electronic_structure_description: The SOC-free cation states along the bend are a 2A-prime, a 2A-double-prime, b 2A-prime, b 2A-double-prime and c 2A-prime. SOC strongly mixes/distorts especially the lowest two and makes the ground adiabatic surface anharmonic; b 2A-prime/b 2A-double-prime mixing opens two comparable one-photon channels. A pump-created ground-cation bending wavepacket crosses the probe resonances with opposite momenta, and strong-field dressed surfaces produce markedly different dissociation probabilities for left- versus right-moving packets.
Other: The multistate CAS model confirms the simpler fitted TDDFT mechanism but resolves essential state mixing. Its neutral-to-cation vertical IP is 0.4 eV below the DFT value/experiment, plausibly because the neutral is state-specific while the cation is five-state averaged; resonance tuning compensates this in dynamics. Both models give a roughly 350 fs/95 cm^-1 wavepacket period and FC distribution centered near vibrational quantum 7 with about five-quanta FWHM. Explicit SOC splits the nominal b-state resonance into locations u=0.21 and 0.45 a.u.; strong probe fields create dressed-state reflection/barrierless transfer, Stark population of state 2, and near-three-photon access to state 5. More than two cation states are required for detailed dynamics even though the two-surface DFT model captures the main modulation.

electronic_structure_description: Compact CASSCF-a is unbalanced: four active orbitals are doubly occupied, one singly occupied, and only one antibonding orbital is empty, yielding neutral Re=1.789 angstrom and omega=603 cm^-1. Adding five Br 4d correlators gives CASSCF-b Re=1.740 and 709 cm^-1, close to experiment, because 4d occupations reach about 0.016 and recover d-p/pi-p backbonding. CASMP2/ECT+(2df) gives neutral 1.726 angstrom/720 cm^-1 and BrO- 1.828/598; CASPT2 with Br 3d correlation gives 1.722/715. method: state-specific CASSCF geometry optimization for S0, S1, and T1; CIS transition electronic dipole moments; crossed-molecular-beam photofragment translational spectroscopy with forward convolution
software: Gaussian 98 revision A.9 for CASSCF and CIS; CMLAB2/KELVIN for beam-spectrum analysis

active_space_protocol: The identical state-specific CAS(8,7) is used to optimize S0, the first singlet excited state S1, and T1 for each meta/ortho/para isomer without symmetry restrictions. The paper reports no state averaging, root weights, or post-CASSCF dynamic-correlation correction. CIS/6-311G* is a separate single-reference calculation for transition-dipole direction, not the source of the recorded CAS.

electronic_structure_description: For all isomers, S0-to-S1 shortens C-Cl and C-CH3 while lengthening the aromatic C-C framework; orbital analysis assigns the transition predominantly as pi-to-pi*. Meta and ortho T1 retain bound C-Cl bonds (figure values: meta 1.779 angstrom versus S0 1.750; ortho 1.754 versus S0 1.782). Para T1 is qualitatively dissociative: C1-Cl=3.925 angstrom, an alternative C2-Cl contact=3.636 angstrom, and the C1-Cl direction leaves the ring plane by 54.4 degrees, suggesting coupled Cl migration/bond cleavage.
Other: CIS S0-to-S1 transition-dipole/C-Cl angles evaluated at S0/S1/T1 geometries are meta 23.0/22.8/17.8 degrees, ortho 6.1/26.6/25.7, and para 54.3/54.2/63.0, matching positive experimental anisotropy for meta/ortho and negative para anisotropy. At 266 nm, meta has beta=+0.5+/-0.2 and mean translation 3.15 kcal mol^-1 (28% of available energy); para beta=-0.6+/-0.2 and 3.28 (29%). Ortho requires two channels: about 60% slow o-tolyl+Cl with beta=+0.7+/-0.2, 2.06 kcal mol^-1 (18%), and 40% fast proposed benzyl+Cl with beta=+0.1+/-0.1, 5.09 (46%). The source proposes meta predissociation through T1 or internal conversion, direct dissociation on repulsive para T1, and for the ortho fast channel pre-dissociation H transfer to 1-methylene-2-chloro-3,5-cyclohexadiene (MCC) followed by Cl loss. Ortho S0 has a reported intramolecular Cl...H contact of 2.651 angstrom, suggested to facilitate transfer.

electronic_structure_description: The full-pi CASSCF wavefunctions describe alternating positive and negative carbon 2p_pi spin polarization localized most strongly near the radical center, together with increasing C-C bond-length alternation toward the chain ends. Relative CASSCF spin populations (largest positive site normalized to 1) are C3: terminal 1.000, central -0.343; C5: C1 0.75, C2 -0.31, C3 1.00; C7: C1 0.64, C2 -0.30, C3 1.00, C4 -0.42; C9: C1 0.47, C2 -0.24, C3 0.81, C4 -0.39, C5 1.00. The CASSCF distributions are qualitatively close to RCCSD(T) benchmarks, while both DFT functionals delocalize spin too evenly and UHF is severely spin contaminated.

For allyl, CASSCF also gives central C-H 1.078 angstrom, averaged terminal C-H 1.074 angstrom, and the tabulated C-C-C angle 124.7 degrees. The authors use experimental EPR hyperfine ratios through the McConnell relationship to benchmark carbon spin-density ratios: full-pi CASSCF is good qualitatively, RCCSD(T)/UCCSD(T) are closest for C3-C7, and absolute ab initio proton hyperfine constants can still be poor. CASSCF C11 and C13 results provide the largest feasible multireference benchmarks; the paper's C41H43 neutral-soliton calculations use only ROHF/UHF/BLYP/B3LYP and are therefore context, not a CAS entry. Those large-chain DFT calculations overestimate the experimental 18-carbon soliton half-width, whereas ROHF makes it too short. No spin-orbit Hamiltonian or spin-spin term is included.

active_space_protocol: Geometry tests used CASSCF(7,7), CASSCF(13,13), CASSCF(15,13), and CASSCF(19,15). The limited (7,7) space incorrectly gives a nonplanar short-bond structure; enlarging the space restores planarity but leaves a strong active-space dependence in the central O-O distance. MRCI geometry optimization used CASSCF(13,13) orbitals, while the reported CASPT2 geometry used CAS(13,11). CASPT2 and MRCI+Q stability calculations used a CASSCF(19,15) orbital set and included all valence electrons in the correlated multireference treatment.

electronic_structure_description: Planar trans-HO3 has an X 2A-double-prime ground state with the stated configuration 10a-prime^2 2a-double-prime^2 3a-double-prime^1. The singly occupied 3a-double-prime natural orbital has occupation 1.02. The long central O-O linkage forms through sigma interaction of one O2 unpaired electron with the HO unpaired electron and also gains weak pi character from O2-pi/lone-pair interaction, enforcing planarity.
Other: Central O2-O3 distances are 1.459 angstrom at CASSCF(7,7), 1.742 at CASSCF(13,13), 1.660 at CASSCF(15,13), 1.758 at CASSCF(19,15), 1.739 at CASPT2(13,11), and 1.647 at MRCI, versus 1.688 experimentally. The preferred CASPT2 thermochemistry gives Delta E=-6.03, Delta(E+ZPE)=-2.06, and Delta H(298 K)=-3.21 kcal/mol relative to HO+O2 and an estimated formation enthalpy of 6.12 kcal/mol. CCSD(T) stability results are rejected by the authors because T1 diagnostics reach 0.052. At the long-bond AIM critical point, QCISD/MRCI values are rho=0.23851/0.16356, Laplacian=+0.16977/+0.31533, ellipticity=0.12061/0.12671, and energy density=-0.1471/-0.0700 au: not a conventional covalent topology but stabilizing and partly pi-like.

electronic_structure_description: Cis-HO4 has X 2A configuration ...16a^2 17a^1, with singly occupied natural orbital 17a at occupation 1.02. It is an O2+HO2 radical adduct: sigma/antibonding orbitals 16a/18a arise from pairing one unpaired electron on each fragment, while interfragment lone-pair/pi and in-plane pi-pi overlaps add weak pi bonding. The cis conformer also has a stabilizing O1...O4 closed-shell contact and ring critical point, explaining its advantage over trans-HO4.
Other: For cis-HO4, CASSCF(11,10)/B2 gives central O2-O3=1.459 angstrom, whereas MRCI/B1 and QCISD/B2 give 1.805 and 1.691; trans-HO4 QCISD/B2 gives 1.583. Trans is 6.01 kcal/mol above cis at 0 K and the cis-trans ZPE-corrected barrier is 7.65. The reliable dissociation barrier is 4.31 kcal/mol at CASPT2 and 4.99 at MRCI+Q; the lower CCSD(T) TS2 barrier is rejected because T1=0.053-0.054. QCISD frequencies diagnose weak interfragment bonding: central stretch 438.3 cm-1 cis and 376.1 trans. AIM central-bond rho/Laplacian/H values are 0.15543/+0.31696/-0.0621 au (QCISD), while the cis O1...O4 contact has rho=0.02618 and H=-0.0045 au.

active_space_orbital_description: The valence reference is CAS(4,4): four pi electrons distributed over bonding 2b1 and 1a2 and antibonding 3b1 and 2a2 orbitals. Symmetry-specific excited-state spaces add the relevant diffuse orbitals: one a2 3d orbital for A1 states; four a1 orbitals (3s, 3p, two 3d) for A2; two b2 orbitals (3p,3d) for B1; and two b1 orbitals (3p,3d) for B2. active_space_protocol: A separate state-averaged CASSCF calculation was performed in each C2v symmetry. MRMP treated each electronic state individually. MCQD treated same-symmetry Rydberg states simultaneously, while valence states were computed separately, avoiding inappropriate valence/Rydberg mixing in the effective Hamiltonian. The article does not report state-average weights or a uniform root count.
nroots_per_mult: Multiple singlet A1, A2, B1, and B2 roots spanning valence and 3s/3p/3d Rydberg excitations; exact SA-CASSCF root counts and weights are not stated. Table II reports 13 singlet excited-state entries.
electronic_structure_description: The lowest valence 1B2+ state is predominantly the ionic HOMO-to-LUMO 1a2-to-3b1 pi-pi* configuration (CASSCF coefficient 0.967). The weak 2nd 1A1- valence state is covalent and strongly multiconfigurational, mixing the conjugate 1a2-to-2a2 and 2b1-to-3b1 single excitations, HOMO-squared-to-LUMO-squared double excitation, and some Rydberg character. The higher 4th 1A1+ state is ionic/multireference and is the strongest transition.
Other: MRMP/MCQD vertical energies are 5.19/5.27 eV for the lowest 1B2+ valence state (MRMP f=0.146), 6.42/6.47 eV for the hidden covalent 2nd 1A1- state (f=0.00391), and 8.11/8.16 eV for the bright ionic 4th 1A1+ state (f=0.502). The first 1a2-to-3s Rydberg state lies at 5.62/5.66 eV; three 3p origins cluster at 6.24-6.32 eV, five 3d states span about 6.81-6.97 eV, and the second-HOMO-to-3s state occurs at 7.80/7.81 eV. Dynamic correlation lowers the ionic lowest 1B2+ state from the CASSCF value of 7.74 eV by roughly 2.5 eV.

method: B3LYP and ROHF geometry/frequency calculations; CIS screening/assignment of visible doublet excited states; state-specific CASSCF excited-state gradients projected onto ROHF ground-state normal modes to calculate Franck-Condon resonance-Raman intensities; isotope-resolved time-resolved resonance Raman spectroscopy
software: Gaussian 98 for B3LYP, ROHF, CIS, and CASSCF calculations; REDONG for conversion of Cartesian force constants to local symmetry-coordinate force constants and potential-energy distributions
basis_set: 6-31G* with polarization functions on every C and N atom for all reported electronic-structure calculations
active_space_orbital_description: For the lower visible transition, CAS(3,4) contains 15b3, 15b2, 16b3, and 16b2 orbitals in D2, or 4b1u, 4b2g, 5b1u, and 5b2g in D2h. For the higher transition, CAS(1,3) contains 15b2, 16b3, and 16b2 in D2, or 4b2g, 5b1u, and 5b2g in D2h. These are the smallest converged spaces after progressive expansion through all orbitals of the transition symmetry; the numeric fields record the larger CAS(3,4).
active_space_protocol: CIS first requested four doublet excited states in each D2 model to identify the two lowest transitions with appreciable oscillator strength and their dominant orbitals. Separate state-specific CASSCF gradient calculations were then performed for experimental transition 1 and transition 2 at both D2 and D2h radical-cation equilibrium geometries. Active spaces were progressively enlarged until predicted Raman spectra were stable; the reported CAS(3,4) and CAS(1,3) are the smallest stable choices. The selected configurations have weights close to one.
nroots_per_mult: CIS requested four doublet excited states for convergence; two bright doublet B3 (D2) or B1u (D2h) states were selected and treated in separate state-specific CASSCF calculations.
electronic_structure_description: The open-shell radical cation has 12 pi and two n orbitals, with the two highest-energy orbitals of n type. Both strong visible states are nearly pure one-electron pi-pi* doublet transitions. In D2h, state 1 is chiefly 4b1u(beta)-to-4b2g(beta) and state 2 chiefly 4b2g(alpha)-to-5b1u(alpha); their CIS coefficients are 0.933 and 0.844. For model 2, 6-s-cis PSB has lambda_max 385 nm at SA-CASSCF, 392 nm at MRCI and 393 nm after Davidson correction; 6-s-cis-11-cis gives 387, 394 and 395 nm. The corresponding RPA values are 405 and 406 nm. Longer model 4 gives MRCI values of 493 and 497 nm for the same two isomers, demonstrating the large red shift with conjugation length.

RPA and MRCI differ by at most about 3% in the reported benchmarks, motivating RPA for the much larger real chromophores. The benchmark also shows why truncated models are hazardous: adding conjugated double bonds lengthens nominal single bonds, shortens double bonds through delocalization and shifts absorption strongly. The full retinal/SB/PSB structures, vibrational frequencies, isomer stabilities, torsional frontier-orbital curves, solvent microclusters and full-system absorption maxima are B3LYP, MP2, CIS or RPA results—not CASSCF/MRCI—and are not represented as separate multireference rows. electronic_structure_description: Furan is closed-shell 1A1. Direct C-O opening gives triplet 3A'' L-furan (structure 4) 322 kJ mol^-1 above furan at CASPT2/0 K and singlet biradical structures near 370-371 kJ mol^-1; the lowest singlet is sigma1pi1 rather than the higher closed-shell carbene-like sigma2 state. The viable minor channel proceeds through 1,2-H-transfer TS20 (280), cyclic singlet carbene 21 (264), ring-opened singlet biradical 23 (309), and C-C fission TS24 (352) to ketene+acetylene (225 kJ mol^-1). The dominant channel proceeds through alternative H-transfer TS25 (288), cyclic carbene 26 (279), formyl-allene intermediates 28/30 (130/118), and concerted TS31 (279) to CO+propyne (129). All values are CASPT2/cc-pVTZ plus CASSCF ZPVE relative to furan at 0 K.
Other: The direct singlet/triplet ring-opening routes have only about 0.1/7.6 s^-1 upper-bound rates at 1400 K and are excluded from the kinetic model. The ketene+acetylene cyclic-carbene route is 234 s^-1 and the formyl-allene route 629 s^-1 at 1400 K; their multistep Arrhenius fits are approximately 1.5x10^15 exp(-344 kJ mol^-1/RT) and 5.94x10^13 exp(-294.1 kJ mol^-1/RT) s^-1. Formyl allene decomposes overwhelmingly to CO+propyne rather than HCO+propargyl. A separate formyl-propyne route has TS34 at 356 kJ mol^-1 and only 2.8 s^-1. Methyl abstraction has 73/76 kJ mol^-1 0-K barriers to 2-/3-furyl, a combined 9.7x10^13 exp(-96.9 kJ mol^-1/RT) rate, and explains methane despite 506/514 kJ mol^-1 furan C-H bond enthalpies. The fitted model uses 82 reactions and reproduces shock-tube furan/major-product profiles; it slightly changes the dominant initiation activation energy from 294.1 to 292.9 kJ mol^-1, lowers the minor-channel A factor from 1.5x10^15 to 9.0x10^14 s^-1, and lowers the abstraction activation energy by 9 kJ mol^-1. CASPT2 underbinds triply bonded products, overestimating CO+hydrocarbon and ketene+acetylene reaction enthalpies by about 25-30 kJ mol^-1 versus experiment, so G2(MP2) is better for those closed-shell thermochemical balances. Conversely, CASPT2 is preferred at biradical/bond-fission structures where Q1 is large and single-reference methods collapse or disagree.

active_space_orbital_description: Orbital-count notation (sigma, pi_x, pi_y): (222) = 6 orbitals for an X-state-only test; minimum two-state (322) = three sigma plus two orbitals in each pi component, including sigma and pi correlating orbitals and diffuse 3s-sigma; (422)/(522) add sigma orbitals; (333) adds an oxygen-localized diffuse pi pair; (433) adds another sigma; balanced (344) adds the fourth, nitrogen-centered diffuse pi pair. active_space_protocol: The principal valence calculations used 7 active/correlated electrons. Equal-weight SA-CASSCF over X 2Pi and A 2Sigma+ was compared with separate state optimizations. Tested spaces were 7e-(322), -(422), -(522), -(333), -(433), and -(344), plus an X-only 7e-(222) test. The 11e-(522)-2s variant included 2s correlation. MRCI reference occupations were selected by maximum spin-coupling coefficient thresholds 0.05, 0.025, and 0.01; final reference lists merged those obtained across r = 1.6-2.4 a0. The avoided crossing at larger r was explicitly outside scope.
nroots_per_mult: two target doublet states: X 2Pi and A 2Sigma+
electronic_structure_description: X 2Pi is the ground valence state and A 2Sigma+ is predominantly Rydberg in the studied region. Increasing diffuse character in X 2Pi at short bond length drives the monotonic increase of the A-X transition moment as r decreases.
Other: The transition-moment function is strongly orbital-basis dependent. Enlarging only sigma space from (322) to (422)/(522) changes little; adding an unbalanced oxygen-centered diffuse pi pair in (333) produces a very small Franck-Condon-region moment, whereas balanced (344), with an added nitrogen diffuse pi pair, restores the magnitude and captures the short-r increase. MRCI removes much but not all CASSCF-space dependence because the selected reference lists are nearly identical and orbital bias remains. The authors identify (344) MRCI(7) as best; its spectroscopic constants are re/omega_e = 2.175 a0/1904 cm-1 for X and 2.009 a0/2421 cm-1 with Te = 42257 cm-1 for A. MRCI(11) closely tracks MRCI(7) with (344), showing 2s correlation is small after accurate valence correlation. At 0.01 threshold, (322) MRCI(11) reached 734395 X-state and 1208479 A-state CSFs, yet transition moments were stable across 0.05-0.01. The computed TMF is nearly linear over the strong-band region and gives A-state v'=0-2 lifetimes of 189.3, 186.1, and 183.1 ns; X-state (344) MRCI(7) gives S(1-0) = 123.9 and S(2-0) = 2.14 cm-2 atm-1, both close to experiment.

method: Full-valence CASSCF correlation-energy decomposition compared with a Hartree-Fock-node/fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo (FNDMC) decomposition. RHF/UHF stability energies supply the spin-symmetry-breaking correction Delta; CCSD(T) extrapolated to the CBS limit approximates exact reference energies. Natural-orbital dynamic/non-dynamic correlation indices were evaluated with CASSCF and FCI, and Slater-Jastrow FNDMC used a single RHF determinant node. Published all-electron FCI and CASSCF energies were shifted to the ccECP energy scale for the cross-method comparison.
software: GAMESS for CASSCF/FCI and natural-orbital indices; Gaussian 09 for RHF/UHF and CCSD(T); QMCPACK for FNDMC
basis_set: CASSCF(14,8) and CASSCF(14,16)/cc-pVQZ; CCSD(T)/CBS extrapolation from cc-pVXZ (X = 3,4,5) with ccECPs; FNDMC RHF orbitals in aug-cc-pVTZ with ccECPs and a 0.0025 au time step. Published all-electron CASSCF/FCI values were adjusted by the all-electron-to-ECP RHF energy difference.
relativistic_treatment: Correlation-consistent ccECPs replaced atomic cores in the CCSD(T)/CBS and FNDMC reference calculations; the paper does not present this as a separate relativistic correction.
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(14e,8o) contains the full F2 valence space. CAS(14e,16o) adds one correlating partner orbital for every orbital in the original eight-orbital valence space.
active_space_protocol: Source-explicit full-valence-versus-extended comparison: CAS(14,8) is crowded, with effectively one empty orbital and maximum excitation degree two for 14 electrons, so it under-recovers non-dynamic correlation toward dissociation. CAS(14,16) adds a complete correlating partner shell and recovers more correlation, but that extra recovery is dominated by unwanted dynamic correlation at shorter distances. The authors judge CAS(14,8) the less inaccurate space for correlation-energy decomposition, not a generally converged electronic-structure space.
nroots_per_mult: Ground-state dissociation/stretching curve only; no state averaging or excited roots are reported.
electronic_structure_description: RHF/UHF instability appears above about 1.4 angstrom, and the HF-node non-dynamic fraction rises toward roughly 50% of total correlation at dissociation. CAS(14,8) follows the qualitative growth but lies below the FNDMC non-dynamic reference in the stretched region because its active space is too restrictive. CAS(14,16) lowers the total energy substantially but exceeds the reference non-dynamic component at all sampled distances, producing non-negligible hidden dynamic correlation, especially at short F-F separations.
Other: F2 shows why lower variational energy is not automatically better for a CASSCF-based dynamic/non-dynamic partition: the double-shell CAS(14,16) is more correlated but less clean as a non-dynamic reference, while CAS(14,8) is undercomplete at dissociation yet less contaminated overall. Both active spaces and the full bond scan are consolidated into one physical-system row.
